 If you’ve been waiting on a new iPad mini, Apple just put a price on it. It’s higher than what you’d pay today.

 Apple announced the new tablet on Monday, with the Wi-Fi model starting at $699. The version with cellular service starts at $849. That’s $100 more than the $599 Apple charges for the current model. Apple already raised that model’s price by $100 in June .
 What the extra $100 gets you
 The biggest change is the screen. The old mini used an LCD panel. The new one uses OLED, where every tiny dot makes its own light. That means deeper blacks and richer colors. Apple says it’s also more than twice as bright as before, which should help outdoors.
 The display grows from 8.3 inches to 8.5 inches. The tablet stays the same size because the borders around the screen are 24 percent thinner. The body shrinks too, down to 5.4 millimeters from 6.3.
 The mini also gets water and dust protection. Apple gave it an IP67 rating. That means it passed testing in about three feet of water for up to 30 minutes. Apple adds that the protection isn’t permanent, and the warranty doesn’t cover liquid damage.
 Apple says a new chip called A20 Pro runs AI features up to 4.5 times faster. The front camera also moves to the long edge. That makes video calls look more natural when you hold the tablet sideways.
 The price could have been worse. Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman said earlier this month that it would land closer to $799. So $699 comes in lower than that guess.
 Is it worth upgrading?
 So is it worth it? That mostly depends on how you use your tablet. If you spend hours reading or watching shows, the screen is the clear upgrade. If you mostly browse the web and check email, a mini you already own may still do the job.
 Extras cost more too. The new Smart Folio cover is $79, and Apple Pencil Pro is $129. Education pricing starts at $649 for the tablet itself.
